clue.text: Oddly squad added no depth, losing power for a way to decide the outcome

indicators.note: oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters only, read across the words squad added no
losing says a letter is dropped from the word depth, and the clue goes on to say what replaces it
for here means 'in place of', so the letter a stands where power was

parts.note: taken as written
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football manager laments that signing new players added nothing to the squad's depth and robbed it of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes letters 1, 3, 5... of SQUAD ADDED NO, giving SUDDEN. 'Losing power for a' swaps the P of DEPTH for A, making DEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied match settled by sudden death ends as soon as one side scores, so it is a tie-break method.

clue.text: One's learned Queen must replace one American lady-in-waiting, for example

indicators.note: must replace tells us one piece is taken out and the royal abbreviation is put in its place

parts.note: a savant is a learned person, one who is learned
A is the abbreviation for American, and one picks out a single such letter from the word
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal household note: a learned courtier must be swapped out for the Queen's own attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: SAVANT has two As; 'one' picks the first, which gives way to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady-in-waiting attends a queen or princess, so she is one kind of domestic attendant in a royal household.

clue.text: See 1 across
One might seek comfort in this tranquil church song

definitions.text: One might seek comfort in this

parts.note: easy, as in calm and untroubled, can mean tranquil
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A worshipper finds comfort in a calm hymn sung in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a churchgoer seeking solace; in fact it is a cushioned armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair built for lounging is where a person settles to relax physically, so it is literally sought for comfort.

clue.text: First of all, probing young journalist asked me about strange bedtime habit?

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every following word, all seven of them

parts.words: probing young journalist asked me about strange

explanation.surface: A cub reporter, nosing about, asks someone about their odd behaviour at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' is not a routine but clothing, as in a monk's or riding habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Habit also means a garment, so nightwear donned before sleeping is a bedtime outfit.

clue.text: Publishing company with marketing men supporting single out on the radio

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting puts the later pieces underneath the first, holding it up
on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word for single out is given by its sound

parts.note: to pick someone is to single them out
AD, an advertisement, is a piece of marketing
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: A publisher and its advertising staff back a single that is being played out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the radio' applies only to 'single out'; 'supporting' stacks the rest beneath it. Picador is a Pan Macmillan imprint, and also a mounted bullfighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Picador is a real British book imprint, part of Pan Macmillan, so it names a publisher.

clue.text: Ultimately, he saw the deal — Jack is first, possibly a diamond

indicators.note: is first puts this letter at the front of the answer, before the rest

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the words he saw the deal

explanation.surface: A card player saw the hand dealt with the Jack on top, perhaps the Jack of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' suggests the card suit, but it is the gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is a precious stone, one example of a gem set in rings and necklaces.

clue.text: Second service goes over net to get game

indicators.note: in a down answer, goes over puts the first pieces above the next one

parts.note: MO, a moment, is a second in informal usage
use, as in being of service or use, means service
to net something is to catch or trap it

explanation.surface: A tennis rally: the second serve clips the net, and the point decides the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis words are a disguise: Mouse Trap is a children's board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse Trap is a long-running board game in which players build a contraption to catch plastic mice.

clue.text: Sample pitted fruit — it's dull

indicators.note: pitted means the stone or core has been taken out, leaving just the outside letters of sample

parts.note: a date is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone tastes a stoned fruit and finds it boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitted' belongs to the fruit in the surface but strips SAMPLE to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried, which shades into staid or dull.

clue.text: Praise whenever I'm darning trousers in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the held letters are read in reverse
trousers as a verb means pockets or takes in, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Someone praises a person who mends trousers whenever times are hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is a verb, takes in; ERIMDA sits inside 'whenever I'm darning' and 'in recession' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to think highly of them, a close synonym of praising them.

clue.text: Smash hit podcast on radio originally — completely timeless and joyful

indicators.note: in an across answer, X on Y puts X after Y, so the shuffled podcast letters come second
originally points to the opening letter of the word radio
smash means break up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
time is T, and completely timeless removes every such letter, both of them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hugely popular podcast goes out on the radio and listeners are delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash hit' looks like one phrase, but 'Smash' is the anagram signal. HIT PODCAST without both Ts leaves HIPODCAS for shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic means ecstatically enthusiastic, a stronger form of joyful.

clue.text: One can be dressed, just like a jack-in-the-box!

definitions.meaning: a ... (noun) is an injury that is dressed with a bandage
... (past of wind) describes a spring toy coiled tight before it pops up

explanation.definitionFit: Injuries are bandaged, or dressed; and a jack-in-the-box is a toy whose spring is coiled by turning a handle.

clue.text: Improvised epilogue about taking heroin

indicators.note: taking means the outer word takes in the drug letter
about means turned round, so the word for epilogue is read backwards

parts.note: a coda is a closing section, an epilogue
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A writer cobbles together a last-minute ending about drug use.
explanation.walkthrough: CODA turned round by 'about' is ADOC, which takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc means arranged for the purpose at hand, off the cuff, which is improvised.

clue.text: After stripping, find adult agents will be generous

indicators.note: after stripping means each word has its outer layer, the first and last letters, removed

explanation.surface: A seedy tale: discover what grown-up agents get up to after undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping 'find', 'adult', 'agents' leaves IN, DUL, GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgent person is lenient and freely gives treats, so is liberal or generous.

clue.text: One with plans for passing Tesla motorcar, say

parts.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density
an estate car (a station wagon) is one kind of motorcar

explanation.surface: Someone with plans to overtake in their Tesla car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' means dying, not overtaking; plans are a will. An estate is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate person dies having left a valid will, arrangements for when they pass away.

clue.text: Crop cutter against visiting hospital department for period of recovery

parts.note: a sickle is a curved blade for cutting crops

indicators.note: visiting means the short letter goes in to stay inside the department

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department
V, versus, means against

explanation.surface: A farmhand cut by a sickle visits the hospital and needs time off.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E, Accident and Emergency, is the British name for a hospital's emergency room; V goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick leave is time off work granted while one is ill, a spell spent getting better.

clue.text: Watch revolutionary go on TV show

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to drag, or drag on, is to go on tediously
ER was a long-running American hospital drama on TV

explanation.surface: Tune in to see a firebrand appear on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a rebel; it reverses DRAG and ER together.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at or observe it closely, which is to watch it.

clue.text: Irregular and liberal — mostly irregular and liberal

indicators.note: liberal can mean free and loose, so the letters are treated freely and rearranged
mostly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A repetitive description of someone unconventional and free-thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition hides different jobs: first 'Irregular' defines, second 'liberal' is the anagram signal. L plus IRREGULA, losing its last R, rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregulars are fighters outside a regular army, which is what guerrillas are.

clue.text: School's covering my burn

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps round the exclamation

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school, with 's as is
cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A school's insurance policy pays out on a pupil's burn.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation like 'My!' or 'Wow!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn something on its surface, singeing it.

clue.text: Content to thank Fed for word game

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside, the letters without its ends

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, a fed

explanation.surface: A thank-you to the setter, Fed, for providing a word game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like the setter's name but is a US federal agent, a G-man.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangman is a guessing game where players find a hidden word letter by letter.

clue.text: Dive and jump, keeping fit inside — quite the opposite

indicators.note: keeping says one piece holds the other
inside describes which piece sits within the other in the surface reading
quite the opposite reverses the stated arrangement, so the word fit goes round the jump rather than inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to leap is to jump

explanation.surface: A gym routine: dive and jump to keep fit indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping fit inside' describes the reverse of what happens, and 'quite the opposite' swaps container and contents. A fleapit is a British term for a shabby cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is a seedy, run-down place, and a fleapit is a dingy cinema or theatre.

clue.text: Formula One is in Monaco on a holiday

parts.note: F1, the motor racing series, written with I for the figure one
est is French for is, the language spoken in Monaco

explanation.surface: The Formula One race is in Monaco during a holiday period.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monaco Grand Prix setting makes 'is' French: EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or public holiday, especially in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Rent kit out — it's of little value

indicators.note: out means wrong or in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hire out a set of equipment, though it is worth little.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket is a small ornament or piece of jewellery, a bauble worth hardly anything.

clue.text: Unaltered under street arrest

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts this piece below the other

parts.note: as is means in its present state, unaltered

explanation.surface: A suspect is held under arrest, still in the street, unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' is not a police matter but a halt, as in cardiac arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of stoppage or inactivity, and an arrest is a stopping of movement.

clue.text: Give clearance

definitions.meaning: give as a noun means capacity to bend or yield, slack
clearance is an allowed gap or margin between parts, a permitted variation

explanation.definitionFit: Engineers call the allowed slack or gap between fitting parts a tolerance; give and clearance both describe such play.

clue.text: Makeover with scope for sex change

indicators.note: a sex change here swaps the male letter for the female letter in the word for scope

parts.note: a remit is the scope of one's responsibility

explanation.surface: A makeover with room for gender reassignment.
explanation.walkthrough: M (male) becomes F (female) in REMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a renovation or overhaul, as of a ship or shop, so a makeover.

clue.text: Partially defrosting potato dish

indicators.note: partially means only part of the word defrosting is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A frozen potato dish is half-thawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss cake of grated potato fried until crisp.

clue.text: Family get together with boat for a base at last — but it can crash

parts.note: stock means lineage or family descent

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the boat goes where the final letter of base was

parts.note: to meet is to get together

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word base

parts.note: an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: A family meeting on a boat as a base, though it might crash.
explanation.walkthrough: MEET loses an E, the last letter of 'base', and ARK takes its place: MARKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial exchange for shares is famous for its crashes, sudden collapses in prices.

clue.text: Silent after vacation with a very loud man

indicators.note: after vacation means the word silent has been emptied of its insides, leaving its ends

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone stays quiet after a holiday with a booming man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a verb: to man a post is to staff it.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a shop or office is to provide people to work it, which is to staff it.

clue.text: Fed gossip about rejected column — it's possibly forged?

parts.note: Fed is the setter, who refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the gossip goes round the next piece

parts.note: to talk is to gossip

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for column is read backwards

parts.note: a row, a line of things, stands for a column here

explanation.surface: The setter gossips about a newspaper column that was spiked, wondering if it was faked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' suggests fakery, but metal is forged by heating and hammering.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalwork is objects shaped from metal, which smiths make by heating and hammering, that is, forging.

clue.text: Soften bulletin describing support from the east

indicators.note: from the east means read right to left, backwards in an across answer
describing here means drawing a line round, so the outer word encloses the support

parts.note: news, as in a news bulletin
a tee is a peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: A news bulletin softens its coverage of aid coming from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' means drawing round, a container signal; 'from the east' reverses the whole across entry, giving the answer from NETEEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten someone is to make them more agreeable, to soften them up.
